codeReview.summary: The feature adds substantial auth lifecycle coverage, but it still misses two required parts of the contract. The new suite does not actually verify the async poll step for signup/signin, and the refresh path still does not prove or guarantee that a new JWT is issued.

issues.description: The full-flow test never exercises the required `202 -> poll -> user created/session exchange` behavior. `stubSubmitter` auto-generates operation IDs as `op_stub_<kind>` (`auth_e2e_test.go:117-129`), but the test manually seeds different succeeded operations at lines 566 and 578 and exchanges `op_signin_alice` at line 582 instead of polling the `operationId`/`pollUrl` returned by signup/signin. There is no call to `OperationByIDRoute` anywhere in this file, so a regression where auth operations never expose the expected `result.user` payload via `/api/v1/operations/{id}` would still pass this feature even though polling is explicitly required by the feature description and VAL-E2E-001/002.

`AuthRefresh` still does not reliably issue a new JWT. `SetAccessCookie` signs tokens using only `sub`, `email`, `type`, and second-resolution `exp`/`iat` claims (`handler.go:112-120`), so a refresh performed in the same second as the original signin/exchange can reproduce the identical token value. The new tests weakened the requirement instead of catching/fixing it: `TestAuthRefresh_WithValidCookie` and the full-flow test only assert that the refreshed cookie is non-empty (`auth_e2e_test.go:420-446` and `:549-645`). That leaves the explicit `refresh ... issues new JWT` requirement and VAL-E2E-019 unmet.

summary: Reviewed commit `c96a16d` plus the worker handoff/transcript for `e2e-auth-flow`. Result: fail. The feature added useful auth and unauthenticated-route coverage, but it still does not verify the required operation polling flow and it leaves the refresh-new-JWT contract unproven and still vulnerable to same-second token reuse.
